source.title: Raise a Child in Large Language Model: Towards Effective and Generalizable Fine-tuning
source.authors: Run-Xin Xu; Fuli Luo; Zhiyuan Zhang; Chuan-Qi Tan; Bao-Bao Chang; Song-Fang Huang; Fei Huang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proposes and evaluates a fine-tuning method intended to improve generalization; it does not test the claim versions about random-label memorization, architecture, optimizer comparisons, batch size, dropout, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal.
record.gate_note: Reports in-domain dev-set scores and transfer results for Child-Tuning, a method designed to improve fine-tuning generalization. These results bear on generalization broadly but do not measure train-test gaps or test any listed version. Cited prior-work results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates its own gradient-masking fine-tuning method and invokes flatter minima as a generalization rationale. It does not test any listed version: its Hessian-based argument does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or rank observed generalization gaps; using AdamW and varying batch sizes across models are not controlled optimizer or batch-size comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that both Child-Tuning variants can improve downstream performance and domain and task transfer, with the task-driven variant generally stronger, and that combining Child-Tuning with prior methods can further improve performance. The record overstates uniform superiority: task-free Child-Tuning lowers RoBERTa's average from 83.99 to 83.90, and Table 2 includes negative individual transfer changes.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tuning pretrained Transformer language models with masked gradients on NLP benchmarks; this paper does not reproduce the listed claim-version experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported performance varies by pretrained model and Child-Tuning variant; the task-driven variant generally scores higher, while task-free Child-TuningF is slightly below vanilla on RoBERTa's reported average.

fits_no_version.finding: Child-Tuning generally improves downstream dev scores and average domain and task transfer scores. Task-free Child-Tuning slightly lowers RoBERTa's four-task average, and some individual domain-transfer results decline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Masking gradients during pretrained Transformer fine-tuning can improve downstream and transfer performance in some settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The theoretical analysis links gradient-mask noise to a Hessian-eigenvalue condition and a generalization bound under Gaussian-noise and SGD assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated assumptions, gradient masking can favor flatter minima and improve a theoretical generalization bound.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Results are dev-set scores rather than train-test gaps; no uncertainty estimates are reported for the averages. The transfer task-generalization values are reported in text alongside a figure, without uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; extracted selected aggregate results rather than each task-level score. Table 1 reports individual task scores and Table 2 reports dataset-level transfer scores, which are omitted because the aggregate findings are already represented.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets and recovery recipes.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a penalty.
Activation dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, and interactions with augmentation or weight decay. Gradient masking is a different intervention.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with measured train–test gaps, and comparative ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing examples selected by label memorization influence versus removing random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted baseline and result values agree with the supplied text. These rows are method-performance results suitable for fits_no_version, not claim-verdict evidence. Their states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8. Lack of train–test gaps alone would not exclude every version; the decisive issue is the absence of the comparisons and interventions each version specifies.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and test performance on natural labels under the same recipe.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold and test-error trend.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparisons and their tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Measured magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with train-test gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
